name: fak — answer-engine disambiguation terms
description: Search and answer-engine terms for correctly identifying fak, including core concepts, performance-lens leads (automatic context management, cache-preserving compaction, cross-agent KV reuse), localized entry points, frontier-model-launch routing/cache/fallback demand hooks, and agent-security hooks (MCP tool poisoning, lethal trifecta, least-privilege tool access, tamper-evident audit).

hasDefinedTerm.name: fak agent kernel
hasDefinedTerm.description: Disambiguates fak from homophones and acronyms: fak is the Fused Agent Kernel for AI agent tool calls.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: Fused Agent Kernel, agent kernel, AI agent runtime boundary

hasDefinedTerm.name: treat the tool call like a syscall
hasDefinedTerm.description: The project slogan: the model proposes a tool call, the kernel decides whether that effect is allowed.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: tool-call syscall, model proposes kernel disposes, AI agent capability floor

hasDefinedTerm.name: default-deny tool-call gate
hasDefinedTerm.description: A fail-closed capability floor for agent tools; an irreversible call is unreachable until policy allows it.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: tool-call control, capability gate, prompt injection defense

hasDefinedTerm.name: prompt-injection result quarantine
hasDefinedTerm.description: A tool result can be held out of the model context by policy and structure, not just detected after the fact.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: result quarantine, tool result isolation, prompt injection containment

hasDefinedTerm.name: addressable KV cache
hasDefinedTerm.description: A cache design where a kept model run can evict a middle span while preserving bit-exact survivors.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: bit-exact KV eviction, agent memory cache, long-session KV reuse

hasDefinedTerm.name: CUDA kernel vs agent kernel
hasDefinedTerm.description: Disambiguates the three senses of kernel around fak: the OS-metaphor agent kernel (the reference monitor that adjudicates tool calls), the compute-kernel arithmetic path, and the literal __global__ CUDA kernels in the GPU backend.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: what is a CUDA kernel, CUDA kernel vs OS kernel, tensor cores vs CUDA cores, agent kernel disambiguation

hasDefinedTerm.name: long-session prompt cache
hasDefinedTerm.description: The cost problem fak targets: a long agent session should keep a provider prompt-cache prefix byte-identical.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: prompt-cache discount, Claude Code token savings, set-and-forget token savings

hasDefinedTerm.name: cheaper way to run AI agents
hasDefinedTerm.description: The 2026 enterprise concern behind cheaper agentic models and "tokenmaxxing": fak measures the prompt-cache saving on a long session instead of vibing it, so the cost claim carries a witness.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: cheaper AI agents, tokenmaxxing, enterprise agent cost control, agentic AI bill

hasDefinedTerm.name: automatic agent context management
hasDefinedTerm.description: The performance-lens pillar behind long sessions that pick themselves back up: on fak's own wire the default-on pipeline plans the resident view, sheds the stale middle while keeping the cached head byte-identical, quarantines oversized results, and pages cold spans back on resume — so nobody hand-manages the window. Honest bound: on a borrowed harness wire fak measures the harness's own compaction but does not yet suppress it.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: automatic context management, zero-knob context, agent context window, managed context

hasDefinedTerm.name: cache-preserving history compaction
hasDefinedTerm.description: How fak trims a long transcript without breaking the discount: it sheds the stale middle turns while keeping the provider's cached prefix byte-identical, unlike summarize-and-discard which rewrites the middle and busts the cache. The witnessed figure is per-fire — about a third of a turn's context trimmed each time compaction fires on the longest measured session — never a re-counted session sum.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: context shedding, history compaction, prompt cache preservation, middle-out compaction

hasDefinedTerm.name: KV reuse across an agent fleet
hasDefinedTerm.description: The cross-agent performance lead, stated with a witness: sharing the model's KV work across a multi-agent fleet does measured less work than re-running each agent — about 4.1x less work than a tuned per-agent baseline on a 50-turn by 5-agent run, and up to 6.95x prefill reuse up the model ladder, each number tracing to a committed benchmark artifact rather than a vibe.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: KV cache reuse, multi-agent fleet, agentic cache benchmark, cross-agent prefix reuse

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent runtime
hasDefinedTerm.description: A provider-operated application runtime that owns and executes an AI agent loop. In fak this is the emerging native path, fak serve --native; it is distinct from the mature fak serve AI-gateway path that governs model traffic.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: managed AI agent runtime, provider-managed agent, managed agent platform

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed AI agent
hasDefinedTerm.description: An AI agent whose loop is hosted and operated by an agent application runtime rather than driven entirely by the caller. fak's native runtime is real but emerging; the gateway runtime remains its mature default.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: hosted AI agent, provider hosted agent, fully managed AI agent

hasDefinedTerm.name: hosted agent runtime
hasDefinedTerm.description: Runtime infrastructure that hosts the agent loop, model calls, and tool-call cycle. This names the application-runtime role, not an inference endpoint or a client SDK.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: hosted agent execution, AI agent hosting, agent execution runtime

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent execution
hasDefinedTerm.description: Execution of the model-and-tool loop inside a managed agent runtime, including the checkpoint where proposed tool effects cross the kernel boundary. It does not mean that the model provider automatically governs every tool effect.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: managed agent loop, agent execution platform, managed agent service

hasDefinedTerm.name: agent runtime vs AI gateway
hasDefinedTerm.description: An agent runtime owns the application loop; an AI gateway governs model traffic. fak exposes both roles from one binary as fak serve --native and fak serve, so the deployment question starts by naming which runtime is meant.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI gateway vs agent platform, agent runtime vs inference gateway, managed agent vs AI gateway

hasDefinedTerm.name: agent SDK vs managed runtime
hasDefinedTerm.description: An agent SDK is code used to build or call an agent; a managed runtime is the deployed service that executes its loop. fak can be embedded as a Go package or run as the native agent application runtime.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: agent SDK vs runtime, agent framework vs managed service, client SDK vs agent runtime

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent infrastructure
hasDefinedTerm.description: The runtime layer that operates agent loops and their model-and-tool execution path. For fak, the native managed-agent surface is emerging and should not be confused with the production-mature gateway and guard surfaces.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent infrastructure, agent runtime infrastructure, managed agent stack

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent platform
hasDefinedTerm.description: A platform that hosts or operates agent application loops. The phrase should identify who owns loop execution, tool effects, and runtime state rather than collapsing an agent SDK, model endpoint, and AI gateway into one product category.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent platform, hosted agent platform, managed agent runtime platform

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent operations
hasDefinedTerm.description: Operating agent loops requires observable allow, deny, quarantine, and revocation decisions at the tool boundary. fak defines those governance operations without claiming to be a complete hosted operations suite.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent operations, agent runtime operations, managed agent ops

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent orchestration
hasDefinedTerm.description: The runtime responsibility for driving an agent's model-and-tool loop. fak's emerging native runtime owns one loop; broader multi-agent workflow scheduling is a separate orchestration concern.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent orchestration, agent loop orchestration, hosted agent orchestration

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent control plane
hasDefinedTerm.description: An out-of-agent enforcement layer that can govern, pause, or refuse agent effects. fak supplies a runtime checkpoint and capability floor; it does not claim every fleet-management feature implied by a full enterprise control plane.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent control plane, agent runtime control plane, agent enforcement plane

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent governance
hasDefinedTerm.description: Policy enforcement for agent tool calls and results at a runtime boundary the model cannot bypass. The governance contract covers observable decisions and revocation, not merely a prompt-level safety instruction.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent governance, agent runtime governance, managed agent policy

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent observability
hasDefinedTerm.description: Audit evidence for runtime decisions across proposed calls, returned results, quarantine, and revocation. This is tool-boundary observability; it is not a claim that fak replaces a general telemetry platform.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent observability, agent runtime monitoring, managed agent audit logs

hasDefinedTerm.name: managed agent deployment
hasDefinedTerm.description: Deployment of a service that owns agent-loop execution, distinct from deploying only an inference gateway or shipping a client SDK. fak exposes the emerging native loop and mature gateway roles from one binary.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: deploy AI agents, agent runtime deployment, hosted agent deployment

hasDefinedTerm.name: enterprise managed agents
hasDefinedTerm.description: Managed agents deployed with runtime enforcement, non-human identity, audit, and cost controls. fak ships part of that enforcement substrate and labels incomplete enterprise packaging rather than presenting the entire stack as finished.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: enterprise AI agents, managed enterprise agents, enterprise agent runtime

hasDefinedTerm.name: serverless agent runtime
hasDefinedTerm.description: A deployment model where provider infrastructure starts and operates agent execution on demand. fak defines the agent-runtime boundary but does not claim that the open-source binary itself is a hosted serverless service.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: serverless AI agent, on-demand agent runtime, managed serverless agents

hasDefinedTerm.name: agent as a service
hasDefinedTerm.description: A hosted service interface backed by an operated agent loop, rather than a raw model endpoint. fak can supply the runtime boundary but is software you deploy, not a vendor-hosted agent service.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: AI agent as a service, hosted agent service, managed agent API

hasDefinedTerm.name: cost-aware model routing for agents
hasDefinedTerm.description: Route the expensive model only to the aspect that needs it, while cheaper calls and retries stay governed.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: model routing for agents, per-call model routing, LLM router complement

hasDefinedTerm.name: Claude Fable 5 model routing
hasDefinedTerm.description: A current demand hook for the general problem fak handles: high-cost frontier models make per-call routing and budget-aware fallback matter.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: Fable 5 cost-aware routing, frontier model routing, Claude Fable 5 agent routing

hasDefinedTerm.name: Fable 5 refusal fallback

hasDefinedTerm.keywords: Claude Fable 5 fallback, frontier model fallback, refusal handling

hasDefinedTerm.name: frontier model prompt-cache cost

hasDefinedTerm.name: safety classifier vs capability gate

hasDefinedTerm.name: long-horizon agent kernel

hasDefinedTerm.name: Claude Sonnet 5 agent cost routing

hasDefinedTerm.keywords: Sonnet 5 routing, cheaper agentic model routing, default model cost routing

hasDefinedTerm.name: MCP tool poisoning defense
hasDefinedTerm.description: A poisoned MCP tool description or result is a structural problem, not a detection one: fak wires only the tools you approve, so a description cannot invoke an unwired effect, and a poisoned result is held out of the model context.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: MCP tool poisoning, poisoned tool description, harden MCP server, MCP security

hasDefinedTerm.name: lethal trifecta data exfiltration
hasDefinedTerm.description: Private data, untrusted content, and an external channel are the three legs of agent exfiltration; fak breaks the third by default-denying the egress effect at the tool-call seam and quarantining untrusted results.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: lethal trifecta, agent data exfiltration, prompt injection egress

hasDefinedTerm.name: AI agent least-privilege tool access
hasDefinedTerm.description: Treat an agent like a privileged identity: fak is the capability floor that scopes which tool effects an agent may cause, fail-closed, instead of trusting the model to stay in bounds.
hasDefinedTerm.keywords: agent least privilege, privileged agent identity, agent capability scoping

hasDefinedTerm.name: tamper-evident agent tool-call audit
hasDefinedTerm.description: Every kernel decision can write a hash-chained, tamper-evident audit row; an auditor re-verifies the chain to prove no tool-call decision was dropped or altered — evidence, not a self-report.
